♡Family Today♡

Both teams won. Bills 36, Texans 31, on a touchdown with a minute and change left. Jets 23, Titans 10. Nobody in this family has to be talked into a good mood today. And the weather cooperated: sunny, 68, the clearest day in two weeks. Bills host Detroit Thursday at 8:15 on a short week.
  • Sep 17Bills host Detroit — Thursday night, 8:15
  • Sep 26Harvest Moon, full at 12:48 p.m.
  • Nov 3Election Day
Had a migraine? Say so in the group chat — the day and roughly when — and the paper will mark it on the Barograph. Enough entries and we will know what the glass does before one hits.

☰The Barograph · 14120☰

High · 61/100
30.15″
↑ up sharply overnight
The biggest jump yet 30.15 this morning, up twenty-seven hundredths overnight — the largest single-day rise since the paper started keeping the log, bigger even than the one a week ago. That matters because the only two migraines on record came the morning after that rise, not after a fall. Two entries is not a pattern, but it is the pattern the log has so far, so today is worth watching: water, food on time, and the Ubrelvy where you can find it. The barometer levels off and stays high through Wednesday.

✶The Ledger✶

Years since Buffalo won in Houston
20
The Bills had not won a game in Houston since 2006, and Josh Allen had never beaten the Texans on the road. Both of those ended yesterday afternoon at about ten minutes to four.

✶The National Wire✶

1

Hormuz Talks Continue

Iran and Oman are still working on a framework for traffic through the strait. Oil held near $110 and diesel stayed above $6 through the weekend.

2

Treasury Yields at a Nineteen-Year High

Buyers are demanding more to hold U.S. government debt than at any time since 2007. Mortgage rates follow, with a lag of a few weeks.

3

Nepal Presses Its Climate Claim

Kathmandu is seeking $20 million after the glacier collapse that killed more than 1,300. It would be among the first payouts of its kind if it succeeds.

North Tonawanda · A Good Week for the Band

The American Legion Band of the Tonawandas took first at the national concert competition again. The Chamber of Commerce of the Tonawandas is still accepting nominations for its annual awards.

Niagara County · The Bat in Pendleton

The bat found on Dunnigan Road on September 4 tested positive for rabies. Any contact with a bat goes to the county health department, not waited out.

3

Rochester · Fringe Downtown

The Rochester Fringe Festival is on downtown, the region's biggest arts event of the year, and a good share of it free.

★The Marquee★

1

The Emmys, Tonight at Eight

The 78th Primetime Emmys air on NBC, shifted off Sunday for football. The Pitt goes in with 25 nominations; Widow's Bay took eight craft awards last weekend and is the comedy favorite.

2

Jean Smart's Last Run at It

Hacks ended with 24 nominations, a record for a comedy, and Smart has won for all four previous seasons. Tonight is the fifth ask.

3

Spider-Man Still Climbing

Brand New Day sits within roughly $14 million of the all-time domestic record, seven weekends after it opened.

🏈The Gridiron🏈

Monday Morning Quarterback
Bills 36, Texans 31. Buffalo had the ball for twenty-three minutes and won anyway, which tells you how the afternoon went: 409 yards on 52 plays, nearly eight a snap. Josh Allen threw for 334 and ran for two scores, and after Ka'imi Fairbairn put Houston ahead 31–30 with a 58-yard field goal, Allen answered with a 34-yard touchdown to Josh Palmer with 1:41 left. DJ Moore caught a 43-yard touchdown in the second quarter in his first game as the No. 1. The defense forced and recovered two fumbles and sacked C.J. Stroud three times.
Got right: the explosive plays came back. Sixteen and a half yards per catch is a different offense than last year's. To fix: ten penalties for 85 yards, and a run game that managed 4.1 a carry against a team missing its right tackle. Detroit on Thursday will not be as forgiving.
Jets 23, Titans 10. The opposite formula and the same result. New York ran it thirty-nine times, held the ball for thirty-nine minutes, and let Tennessee have the ball for twenty-one. Geno Smith went 19 of 24 for 215 without an interception and was not sacked once. Kenyon Sadiq, the rookie tight end who missed all of camp, scored on a three-yard run in the first quarter; Breece Hall added one in the third. Jason Sanders made three field goals, two of them past fifty.
Got right: Frank Reich's offense looked like a plan rather than a hope, and the line did not allow a sack. To fix: the defense still has not intercepted a pass. That streak now stands at an entire season and one game.

Around the league. Chicago 59, Carolina 37 — ninety-six points in the one o'clock window nobody was watching. Baltimore handled Indianapolis 41–23. Minnesota beat Green Bay 39–22, the Giants took Sunday night from Dallas 28–20, and Detroit needed all of it to get past New Orleans 31–30, which is the team coming to Orchard Park Thursday. Denver at Kansas City tonight.
The AI Editor, graded. Bills 11–6 and the division: 1–0, on track. Jets 6–11: 1–0, ahead of schedule, and the paper will happily be wrong about this one. Ravens over Rams in the Super Bowl: Baltimore won comfortably, the Rams lost by twenty at home. One week in, the pick that looks worst is the one the paper made last.
Next Up
Bills · Detroit at Orchard Park, Thursday 8:15 on Prime. Three days of rest, and the Lions just survived a one-point game in their own building. Jets · Green Bay at the Meadowlands, Sunday 1:00.

⚑The Chase⚑

Larson Survives Gateway
Eighteen caution flags, eighty-seven caution laps, two overtimes, and brake rotors coming apart inside the cars. Kyle Larson came out of it with his first win in fifty-one races, beating Hendrick teammate Alex Bowman by a third of a second. Joey Logano led the most laps and finished third. Denny Hamlin lost a lap to a bad pit stop and salvaged ninth; he still leads, but Larson is now second in the Chase and looks like the problem. Ryan Blaney finished 35th, Chase Briscoe 32nd, Chase Elliott 31st. Bristol under the lights Saturday at 7:30 on USA.

☾On This Day☾

September 14, 1901 — 125 years ago today, William McKinley died of his gunshot wounds in Buffalo, and that afternoon Theodore Roosevelt took the oath of office in the library of a friend's house on Delaware Avenue. He was 42, the youngest president the country has had. The house is still there, about twenty miles from this desk.

✧Question of the Day✧

I go up when the weather calms and down when it turns, and yesterday I did the one thing this paper watches most closely. What am I? Answer below the fold.
Question of the Day: The barometer. It rose twenty-seven hundredths overnight, the sharpest climb in the log.
